verdicts.why: Degree 5 and cardinality 8 are read directly; B swaps the terms and C/D are the sum and product distractors.
DROP TABLE removes structure and data; DELETE, TRUNCATE and ALTER are clearly distinct.
DESCRIBE EMP is the standard command for column names and types; the other options are clearly different commands.
Full mesh of 6 nodes needs n(n-1)/2 = 15 links; 6, 12 and 30 are the standard wrong formulas.
Only C is false: a table has exactly one primary key, while composite keys (D) are valid.
HR and Sales have 2 rows each and Marketing has 1, so HAVING leaves HR 2 and Sales 2; option C is the HAVING-omitted distractor.
(A) and (C) are true, (B) and (D) false; key B is unique.
Hub-III, Repeater-II, Router-I, Switch-IV is the standard mapping; only D matches.
LIKE S% is the only pattern-matching condition for names beginning with S.
Bit < Field < Record < Database gives (B),(D),(C),(A), matching the key.
After USE school, SHOW TABLES lists the tables; the other options name different commands.
WHERE filters rows before grouping and HAVING filters groups; A reverses them and B is the aggregate-in-WHERE error.
(A) and (C) true, (B) and (D) false; key B is unique.
SUM ignores NULL (50) and COUNT(QTY) counts 3 non-NULL values; option A is the COUNT(*) distractor. Judges split on hard vs medium, which affects the label only.
Increasing area is PAN, LAN, MAN, WAN, i.e. (B),(D),(C),(A), matching the key.
int('12a') raises ValueError; the other exceptions are for different errors.
ZeroDivisionError-III, FileNotFoundError-II, IndexError-IV, KeyError-I is the only matching option.
Append mode keeps Hello and adds World, giving HelloWorld; no newline means no separator is added.
read(5) leaves the file position at 5 and tell() reports it; the off-by-one options are distractors.

Key A is correct: f(0) returns -1 after finally prints done, f(4) returns 2 after printing done, and the final print gives -1 2.
